criteria.text: Peanut allergy: mitigation of allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, from accidental peanut exposure.
Patient is 4 through 17 years old inclusive (initial dose escalation; approval criterion 1).
Clinical history of allergic reaction to peanuts (approval criterion 2).
Prescribed by or in consultation with an immunologist or allergist (approval criterion 3).
Serum peanut IgE ≥0.35 kUA/L within the past 12 months and/or positive peanut SPT ≥3 mm compared to control (approval criterion 4).
Used in conjunction with a peanut allergen avoidance diet (approval criterion 5).
Confirmed prescription for auto-injectable epinephrine (approval criterion 6).
History of esophagitis or other eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease (denial criterion 3).

History of mast cell disorder, including mastocytosis, urticaria pigmentosa, chronic idiopathic or physical urticaria beyond simple dermatographism (e.g. cold or cholinergic urticaria), or hereditary/idiopathic angioedema (denial criterion 4).
History of severe/life-threatening anaphylaxis or anaphylactic shock within 60 days of screening (denial criterion 5).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Palforzia Criteria Version 1; Original 09/28/2020; Approval 11/20/2020; Effective 01/11/2021.

Encoded: closed peanut allergy indication, approval criteria 1–6 and denial criteria 2–5. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria. Initial dose escalation age band is 4–17 inclusive; the source states up-dosing and maintenance may continue at age 4 and older.
Testing: either qualifying serum peanut IgE ≥0.35 kUA/L within 12 months or positive peanut SPT ≥3 mm compared to control suffices; both may qualify. The source specifies no SPT recency limit.

Cautions (notes only): Palforzia can cause anaphylaxis; patients should be trained to use injectable epinephrine. Monitor for eosinophilic esophagitis and discontinue if suspected. Observe during and after initial dose escalation and the first dose of each up-dosing level for at least 60 minutes. Consider dose modification or discontinuation for chronic or recurrent local gastrointestinal allergic symptoms.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months.
Quantity (notes only): 34-day supply. max_units is null; quantity is not evaluated.
Documentation verification, cautions, duration, reauthorization and quantity require manual review; this pack remains partial.
